findings.summary: The denominator fix (dae2da0) was written as a bullet INSIDE the 1.40.0 CHANGELOG section, but v1.40.0 was tagged at 3db86fc — two commits earlier. So the tagged release's own notes advertised a fix its tree does not contain, and anyone installing from the tag would get the overclaiming `integrity` message while reading that it had been fixed. A CHANGELOG is a claim about a specific tree; writing into a section whose tag already exists makes it a false one.
findings.disposition: Bullet moved out of 1.40.0 into its own 1.40.1 section, which states plainly why it is a patch release rather than an amendment. 1.40.0's notes now describe only what 1.40.0 ships. Retagging v1.40.0 onto the newer commit was the alternative and was REJECTED: moving a published release marker is precisely what the tag-authority discipline exists to prevent, and it would have made the tag unverifiable against what anyone already fetched. Ordering lesson for the release steps: the tag instruction must be the LAST thing issued, and any fix found after it becomes the next patch, never a retro-edit of the tagged section.

findings.summary: `install_into_repo.py --doctor` prints 'STANDING DEMOTION: … sets {TDD_PLAYBOOK_HOOK_EXITCODE: warn} — guards are demoted for EVERY session in this repo' for this repo's settings.local.json. But _common.py:49 sets exitcode's DEFAULT to 'off' (retired to opt-in in v1.32.0), so setting it to 'warn' ENABLES the guard rather than weakening it. The doctor compares against an assumed block-by-default rather than each guard's actual default, so it reports an enablement as a kill switch. Repeated across several release runs in this session and taken at face value once before being checked.
findings.disposition: Left OPEN, not fixed in a release commit — the doctor's H8 output is release-gate machinery and changing what it reports mid-release is the wrong moment. The fix is to compare each env override against that guard's own default from _common.py's table and label only genuine downgrades as demotions (an override that raises off->warn or warn->block is an ENABLEMENT). Recorded because a warning that cries wolf on a correct configuration is how real demotions get skimmed past — the same class as an overclaiming clean message, in the opposite direction.
